Jordan —

Thanks for the clear questions — happy to clarify. TL;DR: we bill billed-token-equivalents for served outputs, with explicit exceptions and credits available for trials and some POC agreements. I'll loop in pricing and billing so you get a sample mapping and confirm trial handling.

Short answers:
- Full cache-hit (response fully served from prefix cache): not billed as a full generation token by default; it's accounted for under a separate "prefetch/served" line in the metering layer and can be zero-rated under a short POC credit.
- Partial hits (KV/prefix partial): billed pro-rata for tokens actually generated; the prefix portion is not recharged as a full generation.
- Trial/POC: we can set cache-hit exemptions so prefetch-served responses don't consume trial credits — we usually toggle a flag at the account level.

I'll send a spreadsheet mapping and the updated rate card shortly — copying pricing & billing.

Rishi / team —

Thanks for the context. Below is the canonical guidance we use with procurement teams; please copy/paste into the procurement packet. I've kept the language non-technical where possible and included an invoice example.

1) Metering primitives (how we show things on invoice)
- "Generation tokens (hosted)": tokens produced by the model runtime. Billed at the listed per-token rate.
- "Prefetch-served responses": responses served entirely from the prefix/prefetch cache. These are recorded as "prefetch-served units" and by default are billed at a reduced metering rate (set in the ratecard) or can be zero-rated for POCs. They appear as a separate invoice line: e.g., "Prefetch-served (units) — $0.00 (exempted for POC)".
- "Partial KV/prefix hits": when part of an output is served from cache and the remainder is generated, only the generated tokens are billed under "Generation tokens". The cached portion is not double-billed.

2) Trial / POC handling
- We can apply an account-level flag that zero-rates prefetch-served units for a specified window (start/end). That prevents them from consuming prepaid trial credit. Configure via the account settings in the console or via the support team for short windows.
- On invoices during the window we show a separate line with quantity and a note: "Prefetch-served (POC exemption)" and $0.00 charge. Outside the window, normal metering applies.

3) Committed plans and discounting guidance
- For committed monthly/annual plans we recommend structuring the commitment around billed-generation tokens (not prefetch-served units). Rationale: commitments are for generated work; prefetch hits are workload efficiency gains and should not count toward the committed burn.
- Discounting: offer the customer a blended effective rate that factors in expected cache hit rate. Example: if expected 30% prefetch hit, commit X tokens at Y% discount so net cost meets target.
- Commercial concession: for sales acceleration we typically offer a one-time engineering credit plus a 60–90 day prefetch zero-rating for POCs. If they commit to a Dedicated reservation within 90 days, apply a one-time credit equal to 10% of first 3 months' committed spend.

4) Example invoice snippet (simplified):
- Generation tokens (hosted) — 1,200,000 tokens — $0.0008/token — $960.00
- Prefetch-served (POC exemption) — 300,000 units — $0.00 — $0.00
- Partial-generation adjustments — 45,000 tokens — $0.0008/token — $36.00
- Subtotal: $996.00

5) Next steps for Rishi
- Send the attached sample-invoice-mapping.xlsx to the customer with the language above.
- Steph: confirm you can flip the POC exemption and advise whether we need a support ticket or if Console toggle is sufficient.
- Ben: if Acadie needs faster procurement, suggest the 60-day zero-rate + one-time credit as a standard play.

I've also linked PRIC-482 (internal) with the precise ratecard lines for prefetch-served units and a draft clause we use for procurement docs.

—Karthik
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

Following up with the specifics you asked for and a proposed POC setup. Key points below and I've attached a short mapping and our ratecard excerpt.

Summary for procurement:
- Full cache-prefetch hits: appear as a separate invoice line called "Prefetch-served". For POCs we can zero-rate these so they do not consume trial credits.
- Partial hits: only the portion generated is billed as "Generation tokens". No double-billing.
- For committed plans: commitments are measured on billed-generation tokens; prefetch hits are treated as efficiency and not required to be included in the commitment.

Proposed POC commercial (standard):
- 14-day zero-rating of Prefetch-served units (we will configure account-level exemption).
- One-time $5k engineering credit applied if you sign a 12-month Dedicated reservation within 90 days of POC close.

Attached: sample-invoice-mapping.xlsx (scenario sheets) and ratecard-v2.pdf (excerpt showing prefetched unit rates).
